subject: Initial: GLBA addendum, subprocessors & data residency — EverTrust Bank
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ken Yamada <ken.yamada@evertrustbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: GLBA addendum, subprocessors & data residency — EverTrust Bank

Hi Ken —

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. I wanted to follow up with a concise list of items we typically need to evaluate feasibility for regulated financial customers so procurement/legal can scope an addendum and technical options. I attached a short checklist for your team (redwood-addenda-info-checklist.xlsx).

Key questions for EverTrust:
- Confirm that GLBA addendum is the primary vertical addendum required (any overlap with state-level banking regs to surface?).
- Residency: do you require strict US-only residency (single region), or is US-based cloud with multi-region failover acceptable?
- Deployment model preference: dedicated Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) vs Redwood Private (VPC deployment / customer-managed infra). Any blockers for a Private VPC pattern?
- Subprocessors: do you need an initial list up front, or is an on-demand roster and 30-day notice acceptable? Any prohibited subprocessors (e.g., offshore support vendors)?
- Controls & evidence: SOC 2 Type II report, pen test summary, encryption at rest/in transit, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) — which are mandatory vs preferred?
- Retention & logging: retention windows (we commonly see 30–90 days; banking teams sometimes require longer audit logs). What is your retention requirement for query/interactions and logs?

Proposed next steps / timeline from our side:
- We can provide an initial subprocessor roster and SOC2/pen-test artifacts within 3 business days.
- If you prefer a Private VPC or Dedicated instance, we’ll task Solutions to scope infra feasibility and a high-level cost delta (5–7 business days).
- Legal can draft a narrow GLBA addendum once we confirm residency & subprocessors (7–10 business days after scope).

Can you confirm the items above and attach any internal RFI/DPA redlines you’d like us to review? If easier, we can set a 30-minute sync with your procurement and privacy leads this week.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internally to keep this moving.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Ken Yamada <ken.yamada@evertrustbank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: EverTrust Bank Legal <legal@evertrustbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: GLBA addendum, subprocessors & data residency — EverTrust Bank

Ben —

Thanks for the clear list. A few clarifications from procurement/legal side:

- Addendum scope: GLBA addendum is required. We do not anticipate HIPAA/FERPA for this engagement (purely financial data), but we will confirm if any regulated partner data flows trigger additional clauses.
- Residency & deployment: EverTrust requires US-only data residency for production PII; for high-sensitivity workloads we require a single-region footprint (US-East-1) with no cross-region backups that store plaintext customer data. We prefer Private (VPC) deployment or dedicated capacity; multi-tenant hosted is disfavored for production.
- Subprocessors: we require an initial subprocessor roster and notification of changes at least 30 days prior. Offshore personnel with access to production data will be a negotiation point — list any support/ops vendors that have potential access.
- Controls: SOC 2 Type II, recent pen test summary (last 12 months), and attestations for encryption-in-transit and at-rest are mandatory. Support for customer-managed KMS is strongly preferred (for on-prem/VPC deployments).
- Logging & retention: for transactional audit trails we need 7 years of immutable logs for specific regulated products; for model interaction logs we would consider a shorter retention with clear segmentation. Please propose retention SLAs for each data class.

I attached our internal RFI (EverTrust_RFI_for_AI_v1.docx) — it has the procurement checklist and the legal redline preferences. Please review and let me know if we should jump on a call — I can loop my procurement and privacy folks.

Ken
Ken Yamada
Sr. Procurement Manager, Vendor Risk & Compliance
EverTrust Bank
ken.yamada@evertrustbank.com

Ben / Karthik —

Looping internal next steps after Ken’s reply. Summary and proposed ownership:

Summary of customer asks (EverTrust):
- GLBA addendum required; confirm no HIPAA/FERPA scope (Ken will flag if any partner data triggers it).
- US-only production residency; preference for Private VPC or Dedicated; single-region (us-east-1) requirement for certain workloads.
- Initial subprocessor roster required + 30-day change notice; offshore access will be sensitive.
- Mandatory evidence: SOC 2 Type II, pen-test summary (<12mo), encryption at-rest/in-transit. Customer-managed KMS preferred.
- Retention: 7-year immutable audit logs for transactional products; model logs negotiable.

Action items & owners:
- Laura: draft a narrow GLBA addendum template and initial response memo to procurement (ETA: 7 business days).
- Karthik: validate Private VPC and Dedicated deployment feasibility for single-region us-east-1, plus a high-level runbook for meeting 7-year logging (ETA: 5 business days).
- Ben: coordinate with EverTrust to confirm whether any third-party partner data will fall into scope and schedule a 30-minute call with their procurement/privacy team if needed (ETA: schedule this week).
- Ops (cc in later thread): prepare subprocessor roster and filtered SOC2/pen-test artifacts for redaction as necessary (ETA: 3 business days).

Please confirm ownership and if those timelines are realistic. Karthik, if there are specific blockers for immutable 7-year logs within a VPC pattern (cost/retention architecture), flag them so Laura can narrow the addendum language.

Thanks — I’ll start the addendum draft and share a first pass for internal review.

Best,
